strategies.name: S1: Calogero variable-phase reduction to a monotone multi-channel control problem, certified with an occupation-measure (Vinter LP / Lasserre moment-SOS) lower bound
strategies.cards: P4 (primary; B = 0 headline, B > 0 via frequency-decoupled k-robust floors); P1 restricted to radial designs
strategies.claim: Imported theorems: Calogero's variable-phase equation for potential scattering, and the occupation-measure characterisation of relaxed optimal control. The latter says the occupation-measure LP equals the relaxed OCP value (Vinter 1993), and the Lasserre-Henrion-Prieur-Trelat 2008 moment-SOS hierarchy converges to it from below. For TM, PEC core radius a, eps(r) in [1, eps_max] on [a, b], mu(r) = eps - 1 in [0, chi_max]. The verified exact identity is sigma_ext(k) = (4/k) sum_n g_n sin^2 delta_n(b), with g_0 = 1 and g_n = 2 for n >= 1, where delta_n'(r) = (pi/2) k^2 r mu(r) [cos delta_n J_n(kr) - sin delta_n Y_n(kr)]^2 and delta_n(a) = atan2(J_n(ka), Y_n(ka)); b_n = (e^{2i delta_n} - 1)/2. Every channel phase is non-decreasing (chi >= 0); the dynamics are pi-periodic in each delta_n, so the state lives on a torus, and the scalar control mu(r) is shared by all channels. Bound: L4(k) = V_S(a, delta^PEC(k)) / sigma_bare(k). Here V_S is the value of min_{mu in [0, chi_max]} (4/k) sum_{n in S} g_n sin^2 delta_n(b) over any channel subset S; dropped terms are >= 0, so every S gives a valid bound. V_S satisfies the HJB equation d_r V + min(0, chi_max grad V . K(r, delta)) = 0 with V(b, .) = cost. The dynamics are control-affine with a convex control set, so relaxed and classical values coincide (Filippov). This matches the weak-* attainment in the card, so the relaxation adds no gap. Band version: every design satisfies sigma(k) >= V_S(k) pointwise, so <sigma>_B >= (1/(k_c B)) sum_j |I_j| min_{k in I_j} V_S(k). The minimum over each sub-interval I_j is certified by treating k as a constant uncertain parameter.
strategies.approach: 1. Derive the 2D variable-phase equation by variation of parameters on (r u')' + (k^2 r - n^2/r) u = -k^2 (eps - 1) r u, using W[J_n, Y_n] = 2/(pi x). The PEC condition u(a) = 0 sets delta_n(a). Already verified: b_n from the ODE matches cloak2d.coeffs to 4.8e-10 (6 random layered designs, n = 0..3). 2. Pose the joint-channel floor as a reachability / optimal-control problem on the N_c-torus with shared control mu(r), and write it as the occupation-measure LP over measures on (r, c_n, s_n, mu), with c_n = cos delta_n, s_n = sin delta_n and c_n^2 + s_n^2 = 1. The dynamics are then polynomial in (c, s, mu) once J_n(kr) and Y_n(kr) are replaced by Chebyshev polynomials in r; the rigorous remainders enter the SOS inequalities as margins. 3. The dual SOS problem finds a polynomial subsolution W(r, c, s) with W(b, .) <= cost and d_r W + mu grad W . f >= 0 for mu in {0, chi_max}; W(a, delta^PEC) is a certified lower bound. Use time-splitting into 4 to 8 radial sub-intervals, each with its own measure, linked by boundary measures, to handle the oscillatory value function. 4. Grow S (N_c = 3, 4, 5, ...) until the bound stops rising. 5. Pontryagin gives bang-bang control with switching function p . K(r, delta), plus possible singular arcs; use it on the design side to roll out DP/SOS-derived policies as adversaries. 6. Band: run the same program with k in [k_j, k_{j+1}] as an extra constant state and average over sub-intervals.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (scratchpad gen_import/: vp_check.py, hjb_torus.py, hjb_policy.py, summary.json). Semi-Lagrangian torus DP, k_c a = pi/2, b/a = 3, eps_max = 6. Two channels {0, 1}: 0.396 a (G = 256) and 0.324 a (G = 512); bare subset 5.044. Two channels {0, 2}: 0.380 a; bare subset 1.834. Three channels {0, 1, 2}: 1.471 a (G = 96) and 1.433 a (G = 64). Rolling out the G = 64 DP policy gives a real eps(r) design that cloak2d scores at 1.004 a on channels 0-2: below the grid value, so grid DP at G <= 96 overestimates and is not a certificate. That design's total is 13.67 a, with n = 3 and n = 4 at 4.52 and 4.42 a (an eps = 6 shell beyond r = 2.71). So the 2- and 3-channel relaxations are provably loose: at most 0.07 and 0.185 of bare, against 0.559 for the best design. Next: dense moment-SOS in cvxpy (Clarabel, SCS fallback) with N_c = 5 to 8 circles plus r. Degree 4 / 6 / 8 moment matrices for N_c = 5 have size 78 / 364 / 1365, within 1 GB. Bessel functions are Chebyshev-fitted to degree about 12 per radial sub-interval with interval-checked remainders. Run the eps_max sweep {2, 4, 6, 12, 20, 50} and b/a in {1.25, 1.5, 2, 3}. Adversaries: DE on L = 16, plus policy rollouts scored by cloak2d.widths. For B = 0.1, use 8 k-sub-intervals with adaptive quadrature of the bare value.
strategies.known_limit_check: (a) The variable-phase equation reproduces cloak2d b_n to 4.8e-10 (done). (b) Each single channel's bound must be about 0, consistent with the baseline per-channel minima of 3.1e-11, 4.8e-19 and 4.2e-10 a. (c) The acausal class mu in [-11, 9] (eps in [-10, 10], valid at B = 0) must give at most 0.0016 a, consistent with the baseline R4 = 0.00029. (d) eps_max -> 1 must recover the bare value (L4 -> 1). (e) The bound must be non-increasing in eps_max and b/a (nested classes). (f) The bound must lie below every adversary, including the rollout design (channels 0-2 at 1.004 a), the L = 16 optimum (3.037 a total; 3.002 a on channels 0-2) and the eps_max = 12 / 20 optima (R = 0.404 / 0.378).
strategies.expected_tightness: The subset relaxations already computed are loose: at most 0.07 of bare for 2 channels and at most 0.185 for 3 channels, against best design R4 = 0.559. That rules out the two-channel Prufer-coupling route suggested in the P4 card. A tight bound needs N_c >= 5, because an outer eps_max shell couples channels up to n ~ k b sqrt(eps_max) ~ 11. If the moment-SOS hierarchy converges at modest degree, the target is a gap ratio below 1.5 at B = 0. At B = 0.1 the frequency-decoupled step should cost only about 4% more, since the baseline shows material, not bandwidth, binds (0.582 vs 0.559).
strategies.closest_prior: No bound exists for P4. The per-channel sum rule (Bernland, Gustafsson & Nordebo 2011; tutorial Eqs. 208-210) is vacuous for |s_n| = 1. Monticone & Alu 2016 (Eq. 218) is a heuristic, channel-independent circuit estimate. Methods imported: Calogero, Variable Phase Approach to Potential Scattering (1967); Vinter, SIAM J. Control Optim. 31, 518 (1993); Lasserre, Henrion, Prieur & Trelat, SIAM J. Control Optim. 47, 1643 (2008).
strategies.risk: High computationally, low conceptually. The reduction is exact and verified; the obstruction lives in 5 or more channels, which rules out grid DP on this machine. A low-degree SOS relaxation may return nearly 0 for an oscillatory value function, so time-splitting and degree escalation may be needed. Bessel remainders must be enclosed rigorously. Radial designs only: free-form P1 designs may beat the radial floor.

strategies.name: S2: Poisson-Jensen waterbed (Freudenberg-Looze / Bode sensitivity integral) on the band semi-disk for phase-compensated far-field projections
strategies.cards: P2 (primary: first certified bound for an angle-limited intensity metric); P1 free-form, flat window (lossless, so sigma_ext = sigma_sca; full-circle version); P3 (sigma_ext >= sigma_sca)
strategies.claim: Imported theorem: the Poisson-Jensen inequality for analytic functions, i.e. subharmonicity of log|G| and of log sum_j |G_j|^2. This is the core of Bode's sensitivity integral and of the Freudenberg-Looze Poisson-integral waterbed bound. Take any unit-norm weights w_j in L^2(Theta), orthonormal, and define G_j(z) = int_Theta w_j(phi) T(phi; z) e^{2 i z b |sin(phi/2)|} dphi. The phase factor compensates the earliest causal arrival (-2b|sin(phi/2)|/c) of scattering toward phi from a scatterer inside r <= b, so G_j is analytic and of non-exponential type in Im z > 0, for every design in the class. Let D = {|z - k_c| < rho, Im z > 0}, rho = k_c B/2, with boundary band I plus arc A, and let omega(z0, .) be harmonic measure. For z0 = k_c + i t rho, omega_I = 1 - (4/pi) arctan t. On I, Bessel's inequality gives sum_j |G_j(k)|^2 <= int_Theta |T|^2 = (pi k/2) sigma_Theta(k). Subharmonicity plus Jensen's inequality give L2 = <sigma_Theta>_B / <sigma_Theta,bare>_B >= [2 / (pi k_max k_c B sup_I(d omega/dk) <sigma_Theta,bare>_B)] * exp{(1/omega_I) [ln m(z0) - int_A ln C_A(z) d omega(z0, z)]}. Here m(z0) = certified min over the class of sum_j |G_j(z0)|^2, and C_A(z) = certified max of sum_j |G_j(z)|^2 on the arc. The arc caps enter only logarithmically, which is the waterbed. For P1 use Theta = the full circle, or the linear harmonic-measure form int_I sigma_ext d omega = Im F(z0) - int_A Im F d omega.
strategies.approach: 1. Prove analyticity and the growth bound for G_j: time-domain support of the directional response is t >= -2b|sin(phi/2)|/c, Paley-Wiener, plus the polynomial real-axis growth |T| ~ sqrt(k), which places G in the Smirnov class N+ on D. 2. Subharmonicity of log sum |G_j|^2 on D gives log m(z0) <= int_I log sum|G_j|^2 d omega + int_A log sum|G_j|^2 d omega. 3. Bound the band term above by the sector power (Bessel), and convert the harmonic-measure average into the uniform average using concavity of log and sup_I(d omega/dk) < infinity (the corner density vanishes linearly). 4. Floor m(z0): a Strekha-type Lagrange-dual or SDP relaxation of the QCQP min ||P_w F(z0) phi_total||^2. The PEC object enters through its analytic TM Green's function G_obj (card P1) continued to z0; constant real eps in [1, eps_max] is causal, so it is the physical continuation. Pointwise class constraints Im(E* P) = 0 and |P|^2 <= chi_max Re(E* P) are aggregated over annular subregions. 5. Arc caps C_A: Kuang-Miller / Molesky max-duals at sampled arc points, finite because complex frequency acts as loss, interpolated with Harnack / Cauchy estimates. A cruder a-priori energy bound of order 1/(xy) also suffices, since log(1/y) is integrable against omega near the corners. 6. Optimise over t, J and the w_j (top singular vectors of the restricted far-field map).
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (gen_import/s2_check.py, s2_semidisk.py). Along k = pi/2 + iy, backscatter |T(pi)| grows to 5.1e3 at y = 3, while |T e^{2ikb}| decays to 7.7e-5; the bare PEC's |T e^{2ika}| grows only polynomially, to 1.75. The semi-disk harmonic measure computed through zeta = ((1+w)/(1-w))^2 gives omega_I = 0.6881 at t = 0.25 and 0.4097 at t = 0.5, matching the formula. The Poisson-Jensen relation holds to within 3e-11; it is an equality, because these G have no zeros in D, for the bare, P1-optimal (de_ext_B0.1_L8) and sector-optimal (lossless_sector_B0.1_L8) designs. Next: build the PEC-object dual in the angular-harmonic basis, where G_obj is diagonal in n, with radial kernels on N_r ~ 40 and |n| <= 20. That gives a block-diagonal QCQP; the dual or SDP in cvxpy + Clarabel stays under 1 GB. Sweep t in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, J in {1, 2, 4}, B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3} and Delta in {pi/8, pi/4, pi/2}. Run end-to-end gap ratios against the layered adversaries (R2 = 0.607) and a ceviche free-form sector adversary with near-to-far projection.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) omega_I(t) = 1 - (4/pi) arctan t is reproduced numerically (done). (ii) The Poisson-Jensen identity holds for zero-free G to within 3e-11 on three known designs (done). (iii) Phase compensation: the residual exponential type must vanish with R = b and fail with R = a (done: 12.5 at y = 3). (iv) End-to-end self-consistency: substituting a design's own |G(z0)| and arc values must give a number <= that design's adaptive band average, for every baseline design (P1, P2, P3 files); any violation is a bug. (v) As B -> 0 the bound must go to 0 for the lossless class, which has no protection at B = 0. (vi) Nested sectors give the correct ordering, and Theta = the full circle reproduces sigma_sca exactly (fastcyl.sector_width check).
strategies.expected_tightness: Moderate to weak. The exponent 1/omega_I (1.45 at t = 0.25) amplifies the looseness of the m(z0) relaxation, and for lossless materials m(z0) shrinks roughly in proportion to Im z0 (Strekha's d omega -> 0 behaviour). Expect gap ratios of about 10-100 at B = 0.1, improving at B = 0.3. It would still be the first nonzero certified number for P2, and the first flat-window free-form number for P1.
strategies.closest_prior: Freudenberg & Looze, IEEE TAC 30, 555 (1985), the Poisson sensitivity integral and waterbed; Bode 1945. Strekha et al., PRA 110, 063513 (2024), a Lorentzian extinction dual for a penetrable object only. Shim, Fan, Johnson & Miller, PRX 9, 011043 (2019) state that quadratic powers cannot be continued analytically; that obstacle is sidestepped because log|G| for a linear G is subharmonic. No prior sector-metric bound exists.
strategies.risk: m(z0) may be nearly 0 at small t for lossless chi; then t must grow, which lowers omega_I. Arc caps are needed rigorously over a continuum of complex frequencies. Over-compensation by e^{2iz(b - R_eff)} (the support is smaller than b) costs a factor e^{-2(b - R_eff) Im z0}, mild at these Im z0. Building the PEC-object dual is a substantial new code.

strategies.name: S3: f-sum disk (convex-geometry) relaxation of the electron budget: harmonic-mean floor on Im xi, giving an l1-SOC term in the design-region optical theorem
strategies.cards: P3 (primary; Lorentzian metric M_L exactly, flat window via the semi-disk Poisson identity); the lossless limit cross-checks P1
strategies.claim: Imported theorem (convex geometry plus the f-sum rule): each Lorentz oscillator's unit-strength susceptibility at complex z, 1/(omega0^2 - z^2 - i gamma z), lies on a circle through 0 of diameter 1/(Im z^2 + gamma Re z). These circles are nested and tangent at 0, so by convexity every causal passive multi-oscillator medium with local strength s(x) = sum_j omega_pj^2 and gamma_j >= gamma_min satisfies |chi(x,z)|^2 <= s(x) Im chi(x,z) / y_min(z), with y_min(z) = Im(z^2) + gamma_min Re z. Equivalently Im xi(x,z) >= y_min(z)/s(x), with xi = -1/chi. The budget (1/A) int s <= W omega_c^2 therefore gives int_ann dA / Im xi(x,z) <= Q(z) := W omega_c^2 A_ann / y_min(z). Combine this with the design-region optical theorem in the presence of the PEC core, Im<E_d, phi> = phi^dagger Asym(G_obj) phi + int Im xi |phi|^2, and with Cauchy-Schwarz, int Im xi |phi|^2 >= ||phi||_1^2 / Q. The result is the convex program L_M(W) = min_phi [Im F_bare(k~) + l(phi)] s.t. phi^dagger A phi + ||phi||_1^2 / Q(k~) <= Im<E_d, phi>, plus subregion versions with budget split Q_m, sum Q_m <= Q. Here l(phi) is affine and comes from the reciprocal bare field, and A = Asym G_obj in passivity-consistent weighting; at real k it is sum_n (1/4) psi_n psi_n^dagger, rank one per harmonic. R3 for the M_L metric is >= L_M / M_L,bare (5.52 a). Flat window: <sigma_ext>_B >= [L_M(z0) - int_A U(z) d omega(z0, z)] / (k_c B sup_I d omega/dk), with U(z) the maximum of the same program on the arc. U is finite because ||phi||_1 <= Q(z) ||E_d||_inf, and y_min -> gamma_min x > 0 at the corners. The bound is non-increasing in W because Q grows with W, as the card requires.
strategies.approach: 1. Prove the circle and disk lemma (Mobius image of the line t -> t - z^2 - i gamma z) and the conic-hull step, Caratheodory for sums of oscillators plus the unused share. Repeat it for the Herglotz-weighted form h = z chi, also a single disk, of diameter |z|/y_min. 2. Write the exact design-region optical theorem with the PEC-object Green's function at k~, in the Kuang-Miller passivity-consistent weighting, so the Asym operator is PSD; check this numerically after discretisation. 3. Key step: a perfect single-frequency cloak needs Im<E_d, phi> to equal the radiated term exactly, so any finite Q forces a residual of scattering plus budget-limited absorption. The relaxation is therefore nontrivial although it uses only global constraints. 4. Add Strekha-style subregion constraints with split budgets Q_m (jointly convex quadratic-over-linear terms, ||P_m phi||_1^2 / Q_m) via the Lagrange dual. 5. Uniform window: the semi-disk Poisson identity for the positive harmonic function Im F, with the floor at z0 and caps on the arc, both from the same convex program.
strategies.numerical_procedure: Already run (gen_import/s3_check.py, s3_disk_weighted.py). For 2.2e5 sampled oscillators at k~ = k_c(1 + 0.05i) with gamma >= 0.01 omega_c: y_min = 0.110 k_c^2, and max y_min |chi|^2 / Im chi = 1.00000000, attained at gamma_min. The weighted locus has diameter 5.79468, equal to |k~|/y_min. The f-sum integral int omega Im eps d omega = 2.042035 against (pi/2) omega_p^2 = 2.042035. The W = 0.5 baseline design (lorentz_W0.5_L4_g0.01.json) meets the budget inequality with equality (0.4999 vs 0.4999 k_c^2), so the relaxation is exact for single-oscillator designs at minimum damping. Next: polar grid 32 x 128 in the annulus; phi(r, phi) = sum_{|n| <= 20} phi_n(r) e^{in phi}; G_obj diagonal in n with analytic radial kernels at complex k~; pixel values via per-ring DFT. cvxpy SOCP (Clarabel) with about 1300 complex variables and 4096 abs terms, solved in seconds. Run W in {0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 2, 8}, gamma_min in {0.001, 0.01, 0.1} and B in {0.03, 0.1, 0.3}. Arc caps at about 32 arc points, then the semi-disk weights. Adversary: run_lorentz.py at the same (W, gamma_min, B), also scored on M_L.
strategies.known_limit_check: (i) The f-sum rule is reproduced (done). (ii) The disk containment, the weighted disk and equality at minimum damping are verified (done). (iii) The budget inequality is saturated by the W = 0.5 optimum (done). (iv) As W -> 0, L3 -> 1, with first-order slope matching single-small-inclusion perturbation theory and Lorentz adversaries at W = 0.05 and 0.1. (v) As W -> infinity with real-frequency evaluation, the global bound must go to 0, consistent with perfect single-frequency lossless cloaking being allowed (tutorial Sec. 5.7). (vi) The G_obj discretisation must reproduce cloak2d b_n of a layered design to about 1e-3. (vii) The bound must be non-increasing in W.
strategies.expected_tightness: Best in the budget-binding regime. At W = 0.5 the baseline M_L ratio is 0.907 (5.009 against 5.52 a), and the global-constraint bound should reach about 0.3-0.8, a gap of about 1.1-3x. It loosens at W >= 2, where the eps ~ 4 coating needs no sub-unity eps and the budget barely binds; there it degrades to a Strekha-like constraint-only bound. The flat-window version is weaker by the conversion factor and the arc term.
strategies.closest_prior: No f-sum-budget cloaking bound exists. Strekha et al. 2024 fix chi(omega~) with no budget. Jelinek, Gustafsson, Capek & Schab 2021 use a pointwise loss floor, Re rho >= rho*. Zhang, Monticone & Miller 2023 have f-sum constraints only in an unstructured volume-T-matrix oscillator model (tutorial Eq. 175c). Gustafsson & Sjoberg 2010 give passive-approximation material bounds.
strategies.risk: PSD-ness of the weighted Asym(G_obj) at complex frequency must be verified; if it fails, fall back to the Lagrange dual, which needs no convexity. Global constraints alone may be loose at large W. The flat-window conversion depends on arc caps that grow like Q(z) ~ 1/(gamma_min x) near the band edges, which is integrable but loosens the bound. As gamma_min -> 0 the real-frequency floor vanishes, so the bound measures dispersion cost only through complex-frequency evaluation.
